bugs.error_message: Error: Cannot find package '@testing-library/dom' imported from node_modules/@testing-library/jest-dom/dist/matchers-*.mjs (all 8 vitest suites failed to load)
bugs.root_cause: Installing eslint-plugin-react with --legacy-peer-deps (its peer range caps at eslint ^9.7, project has eslint 10) made npm re-resolve the tree without auto-installed peer deps, silently dropping @testing-library/dom, a peer of @testing-library/jest-dom.
bugs.fix: Dropped eslint-plugin-react entirely (ESLint 10's core no-unused-vars is already JSX-aware, verified with a probe file), then ran a plain `npm install` to restore the tree. 106/106 tests pass.

bugs.error_message: [@stylistic/eslint-plugin-js] This package is deprecated in favor of the unified @stylistic/eslint-plugin, please consider migrating to the main package
bugs.root_cause: The js-only stylistic plugin (v4) was archived upstream in favour of the unified @stylistic/eslint-plugin. Migrating renames the namespace @stylistic/js/* -> @stylistic/*, and the unified v5 changed one default: indent SwitchCase 0 -> 1, which then flagged 48 pre-existing switch statements in src/lib/errors.js and src/utils/periods.js.
bugs.fix: npm uninstall @stylistic/eslint-plugin-js; npm i -D @stylistic/eslint-plugin (5.10.0). Renamed the plugin key to @stylistic and all four rule prefixes. Pinned { SwitchCase: 0 } on @stylistic/indent so the enforced style is byte-identical to before - zero source files reformatted. lint clean, 106/106 tests, build ok.

bugs.error_message: Error: Timed out waiting 120000ms from config.webServer
bugs.root_cause: Vite's default host is `localhost`, which resolves to ::1 first on Windows, so the dev server bound IPv6-only while Playwright's readiness poll knocked on http://127.0.0.1:5175 forever. vite.config.js has no server block, so nothing pinned the interface.
bugs.fix: Pass the interface on the webServer command line: `npm run dev -- --port 5175 --strictPort --host 127.0.0.1`. Playwright's own `port`/`url` options only say what to poll, they configure nothing.

bugs.error_message: Email address "worktime-e2e-a@example.com" is invalid  /  email rate limit exceeded
bugs.root_cause: Supabase's signUp validator rejects placeholder domains (example.com, anything under .test). Retrying across candidate domains then tripped the per-project email rate limit, because signUp is metered against the email quota even when confirmations are off. signInWithPassword does NOT run the domain validator, so probing with sign-in cannot tell you which domains are acceptable.
bugs.fix: Stop calling signUp at all. The two E2E accounts are created once by hand in the dashboard (Authentication -> Users -> Add user, Auto Confirm User ticked) and the suite only ever signs in -- no mail, no metering, no dependency on the Confirm-email or Allow-signups settings.

bugs.error_message: e2e entries.spec.js:26 'every duration notation lands on the right number of minutes' fails only in a parallel run: expect(categoryRow).toBeVisible() times out at helpers/app.js:49 and the page snapshot shows the /login screen.
bugs.root_cause: supabase-js defaults supabase.auth.signOut() to scope 'global', which revokes EVERY refresh token the user holds, not just the calling browser's. auth.spec.js:72 signs in as ACCOUNT_A and signs out; both E2E accounts are shared by every worker, so that global revocation killed the ACCOUNT_A session of whatever test was running concurrently on the other worker. The longest entries test was the usual victim. It passed when run alone because nothing else was signed in as A.
bugs.fix: supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }) in authSlice.js (and the same in e2e/helpers/backend.js so `npm run e2e:reset` cannot do it either). Local scope still clears the persisted session from localStorage, which is all the sign-out test actually asserts. Repro was deterministic with just `npx playwright test e2e/auth.spec.js e2e/entries.spec.js`; green after the fix, and two back-to-back full runs pass 13/13.

bugs.error_message: npm ci fails: `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json are in sync. Missing: @vitest/ui@4.1.11 from lock file (plus its deps fflate, sirv, @polka/url, mrmime, totalist).
bugs.root_cause: @vitest/ui was added to package.json devDependencies during the coverage-reporter work (commits fc0f967 / 10c9b93) without re-running npm install, so the lockfile was never regenerated and the two drifted. Nothing local caught it: node_modules was already populated and `npm run build` never consults the lock. Every clean install did break -- ci.yml and nightly.yml both run `npm ci`, and Cloudflare Pages runs `npm clean-install`, so the deploy could not have built until this was fixed.
bugs.fix: Ran `npm install` to regenerate package-lock.json, then verified `npm ci` succeeds from the synced lock. lint clean, 128 unit tests pass, build clean. Rule: any package.json dependency edit must be followed by `npm install`, with the lockfile committed in the same change.

bugs.error_message: fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/darol81/scheduler.git/': SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate (on git push / ls-remote)
bugs.file: git global config (not a repo file)
bugs.root_cause: Git for Windows 2.46 defaults to the OpenSSL TLS backend, which trusts only its own bundled ca-bundle.crt. Something on this machine terminates and re-signs HTTPS (antivirus TLS inspection or a network appliance), presenting a root certificate that lives in the Windows certificate store but not in Git's bundle, so the chain could not be built. Nothing was wrong with the repo, the remote or the credentials.
bugs.fix: Confirmed the diagnosis non-destructively with `git -c http.sslBackend=schannel ls-remote origin HEAD`, which succeeded, then made it permanent: `git config --global http.sslBackend schannel`. schannel makes Git use the Windows certificate store. Do NOT reach for `http.sslVerify false` -- that disables verification outright instead of fixing trust.

bugs.error_message: GitGuardian: E2E account password committed to a public repository. E2E_PASSWORD defaulted to the literal 'playwright-e2e-pw' in e2e/helpers/env.js, repeated in README.md, manual_work_todo.md and .env.example.
bugs.root_cause: The credential had a convenience default so `npm run e2e` would work with no setup. That default WAS the leak: it is the real password of two live accounts in the production Supabase project, and the repository is public. nightly.yml already read E2E_PASSWORD from a repository secret, so the private path existed all along -- nothing was gained by the fallback. Verified exploitable rather than theoretical: both accounts returned HTTP 200 from POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password against the live project, using the anon key scraped from the deployed bundle. It also partly undid the deployment lockdown -- signups had been closed so nobody could CREATE an account, but two accounts with a published password already existed. Blast radius was bounded by RLS: every policy compares auth.uid() to the row owner, so an intruder was confined to those two empty accounts and could not reach the owner's data; they could still burn quota, change the password to lock the suite out, or call e2e_reset_account() on their own rows.
bugs.fix: Removed the default entirely; loadE2EEnv now throws a message naming .env.e2e.local and the CI secret, because failing loudly is the point. Scrubbed the literal from all tracked files. Kept the two ADDRESSES public -- they are identifiers, not credentials, and must match the allowlist in supabase/e2e.sql. Rotated both accounts (same password: helpers/accounts.js gives A and B one shared E2E_PASSWORD) and verified at the API -- the old value now returns 400 where it returned 200. Did NOT rewrite git history: rotation makes the old value worthless and avoids rewriting a protected branch. PR #17, issue #16.

bugs.error_message: e2e: .env.local must define VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY -- raised even though .env.e2e.local existed and held E2E_PASSWORD.
bugs.root_cause: The two env files are not redundant; they feed different processes, and the error text names only one of them. loadE2EEnv runs loadEnv('e2e', ...) so it sees .env.local AND .env.e2e.local -- but the suite's webServer spawns `npm run dev`, which is Vite in DEVELOPMENT mode and never loads .env.e2e.local. Putting the Supabase values in .env.e2e.local therefore clears this error and then fails all 17 specs, because the dev server boots unconfigured and renders SetupNotice with no login form for the tests to drive.
bugs.fix: Created .env.local with VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (both public by design and identical to the Cloudflare Pages env vars -- they can be scraped from the deployed bundle, so no secret handling is needed), leaving E2E_PASSWORD in .env.e2e.local. Both are gitignored. A second failure hid behind this one: all 17 specs then failed with "browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist" because `npx playwright install chromium` had never been run -- a missing binary that reads like a config fault. After both, npm run e2e passes 17/17 in 26s. README section 3.2 now documents the split.
